summary: A local public office or municipal service where residents come to get a task done: task-first home with today's opening and waits, a searchable services A–Z, dated announcements and an accessibility statement, with an accessibility toolbar on every page.

pages.purpose: Get residents to the task they came for in one step, and tell them what is happening at the office today.

sections.purpose: Text size, high contrast and link underlines for the whole site, at the very top before the navigation.
fields: Which options to offer (text size steps, contrast, underline links)
sections.notes: A labelled region; on phones it collapses to one line that opens the settings so it never pushes the page down. Applies through the kit's tokens (root font size, muted text to full strength, hairlines to solid rules) and is remembered on the device, read after mount to avoid hydration mismatch.

sections.purpose: One time-boxed notice (closures, outages, changed hours).
Ask 'what do you need to do today?', a search that opens the services A–Z, and today's status at the office: open/closed, hours and current desk waits.
alternatives: page-header: a smaller office without live status
fields: Desk names and current waiting times (if available)
sections.notes: The search is a GET form with role=search that lands on the services page prefilled (?q=). Desk waits are a small captioned table; say when they were last updated.

sections.purpose: The most requested tasks, numbered, with large click targets.
fields: Top tasks: name, one-line description, online or in person, link

sections.purpose: Dated, typed announcements (works, closures, consultations, events).
sections.notes: Dates as text, type as a badge with a word, never colour alone.

sections.purpose: Monthly service figures (applications handled, average wait, share online).
fields: Figures with label, month and source

sections.purpose: Address, map, opening hours per desk and how to get there.
The accessibility statement: standard met, known issues, how to report a problem and get an alternative format.
fields: Conformance level and date of last review
Contact for accessibility problems and alternative formats

pages.purpose: Find any service by search, topic or 'online only', and read what it needs.

sections.purpose: Breadcrumb, title and how the list works.
Search (accent- and case-insensitive), a topic switch and an 'online only' filter; results grouped by topic as an accordion.
alternatives: command: a very large catalogue with quick search
sections.notes: Prefill the search from ?q=; a #service-id hash opens that service. Announce the result count in a status region; keep matching tolerant of Turkish characters.

pages.purpose: One announcement with the facts first: when, where, reference, what to do.

sections.purpose: Title, type, publication date and breadcrumb.
The key facts as a definition list (start, end, reference number).
Practical help for residents (alternatives, assistance for elderly or disabled residents).
fields: Assistance offered and how to request it

sections.purpose: Dated updates as the situation changes.
alternatives: activity-timeline: an ongoing disruption with status updates

sections.purpose: Affected streets or areas as a text list, and the official notice to download.

content: Office name, address, map location and parking/step-free access
Opening hours per desk, late openings and holiday closures
Full services list: name, topic, online/in person, documents, fees, processing time, link
Top tasks residents ask for most
Announcements with type, dates, affected areas and official notice files
Accessibility statement: conformance level, review date, known issues, contact
Languages the site and services are offered in

styles.name: civic plain
styles.why: System fonts, a deep civic blue tuned for AAA text contrast in both modes, ruled lists and large targets; for any public body.

styles.name: institutional
styles.why: Neutral, formal look for agencies and directorates that must stay brand-neutral.

pitfalls: Announcements dated or typed by colour only; print dates and types as text.
An accessibility toolbar that only resizes some blocks or overflows layouts; apply it through tokens so everything reflows.
No accessibility statement or no way to request an alternative format.
Live waiting times or hours shown without a 'last updated' time, and wrong on holidays.
Service search that fails on Turkish characters or synonyms (e.g. accented vs plain spelling).
Official notices only as PDFs; put the key facts and affected areas on the page as text.
Decorative motion or low-contrast muted text on a site that must serve everyone.
